profile.address: Crimson View Drive, Daybreak, South Jordan, Salt Lake County, Utah, 84009
profile.reading:
This entry corresponds to a portion of eBay's data center campus in South Jordan, Utah, near the master-planned Daybreak community in southwest Salt Lake County. eBay began developing this site after announcing a roughly $334 million Utah data-center investment, drawn in part by the state's low seismic risk, an existing eBay customer-service relationship in Utah, and a state tax-incentive package worth about $27.3 million over ten years. Construction delivered the first phase, a design-build, roughly 250,000-square-foot, two-level Tier IV facility with about 30,000 square feet of administrative office space, in October 2010, built by general contractor Skanska USA Building with Harris Company handling mechanical systems on a fast-track schedule; the completed building earned LEED Gold certification.

eBay has continued to expand the campus since. Industry and architectural-firm project pages describe it today as several eBay-owned buildings on site, referred to in industry material as the "Topaz" campus, with individual construction phases identified as SLC01, SLC02, and SLC03. One later phase, documented as a data-hall fit-out inside an already-standing building, is described with a combined building footprint of roughly 146,700 square feet, a 42,600-square-foot data hall, and a 10.4-megawatt critical IT load, illustrating the scale of individual buildings on this campus, though this registry entry cannot confirm which specific structure corresponds to which expansion phase.

The campus functions as a computational hub for eBay's core businesses: regional business press covering a September 2013 expansion reported that transaction processing for eBay Marketplace, PayPal, and StubHub runs through this site, and that the newest building at the time drew roughly three-quarters of its required 8 megawatts from on-site Bloom Energy natural-gas fuel cells, with a planned Ormat waste-heat-recovery partnership to generate further electricity from the fuel cells' exhaust heat. Both the data center and eBay's nearby Draper customer-service campus have achieved LEED Gold certification.

No eBay-published document identifies a specific street address, individual building name, or exact power and cooling specification for this precise mapped location within the larger, multi-building campus, so the figures above describe the eBay South Jordan campus as a whole rather than confirming them for this exact footprint.
